questionText:
The relation scheme given below is used to store information about the employees of a company, where empId is the key and deptId indicates the department to which the employee is assigned. Each employee is assigned to exactly one department.

$$\text{emp}(\underline{\text{empId}}, \text{name}, \text{gender}, \text{salary}, \text{deptId})$$

Consider the following SQL query:

The above query gives, for each department in the company, the number of female employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of
codeBlock:
select deptId, count(*)
from emp
where gender = "female" and salary > (select avg(salary) from emp)
group by deptId;
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the subquery
The subquery (select avg(salary) from emp) executes independently without any correlation to the outer query. It computes the average salary of all rows in the emp table, representing the average salary of all employees in the company.

Step 2: Analyze the WHERE clause
The condition where gender = "female" and salary > (...) filters tuples to select only female employees whose individual salary exceeds the overall average salary of the company.

Step 3: Analyze the GROUP BY clause
The group by deptId clause aggregates these qualified female employees by department, and count(*) counts how many such female employees belong to each department.

Therefore, the query calculates the number of female employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of employees in the company.
